blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable task-level supervision, yet offers limited guidance for localizing errors in visual reasoning. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) complements this supervision with dense token-level corrections from a privileged teacher equipped with an evidence-centered visual view. However, the resulting corrections may conflate visual evidence with non-visual shifts induced by linguistic priors, response style, or the privileged view itself. We formalize this phenomenon as privileged-correction contamination: a token-level correction is contaminated when its update direction cannot be consistently attributed to the privileged visual evidence. Directly distilling contaminated corrections may therefore reinforce erroneous token-level updates. To address this issue, we propose reinforcement learning with visually attributable on-policy self-distillation, an evidence-consistent paradigm that augments task-level RLVR supervision with privileged token-level corrections grounded in visual evidence. We instantiate this paradigm with Visual-Attribution Gating (VAG), which uses the verifier-derived advantage as the optimization anchor and validates each privileged correction against the contrast between evidence-present and evidence-degraded teacher views. By admitting only corrections directionally supported by this visual contrast, VAG preserves visually grounded guidance while suppressing inconsistent residuals. Experiments across six visual reasoning benchmarks show that VAG consistently outperforms GRPO and OPSD methods, establishing new state-of-the-art average performance.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an effective
paradigm for improving multimodal reasoning by optimizing policies against
automatically checkable outcomes ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2025 ) .
In GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) , a verifier scores each rollout and group-relative
normalization turns these rewards into an outcome advantage A ORM A_{\mathrm{ORM}} shared by every token. Such supervision is
reliable at the trajectory level, but coarse at the token level: the same
advantage is assigned to every token, regardless of which visual decision
determines the answer. Consequently, RLVR can distinguish successful
trajectories from unsuccessful ones without localizing the visual reasoning
errors within them.

Our contributions are summarized as follows: • We identify privileged-correction contamination ,
showing that dense teacher–student corrections are not necessarily aligned in direction with the visual evidence. • We propose an evidence-consistent paradigm unifying RLVR and OPSD, in

admitting a teacher correction only under sign agreement with a controlled
visual contrast. • Across six visual reasoning benchmarks, VAG consistently improves over

leading closed-source models, while holdout evaluation shows no loss of
general capability. Ablations further validate the proposed attribution
mechanism.

blocks.en: 2.1 On-Policy and Privileged Distillation
blocks.zh: 2.1 政策和特权分离

blocks.en:
OPD supervises student-visited prefixes with a
teacher, thereby reducing exposure bias while supplying dense token-level
guidance ( Gu et al., 2023 ; Agarwal et al., 2024 ; Song and Zheng, 2026 ) .
OPSD replaces the external teacher with the model
itself conditioned on privileged context, such as verified solutions, reasoning
traces, or environmental feedback ( Zhao et al., 2026 ; Hübotter et al., 2026 ; He et al., 2026 ; Jin et al., 2026 ) . Because the
student cannot access this context at inference time, the resulting
teacher–student gap may conflate task-relevant knowledge with leakage or
stylistic artifacts ( Yang et al., 2026 ; Pan et al., 2026 ; Shen et al., 2026 ) . In multimodal
reasoning, privileged views instead expose localized evidence that global image
processing tends to lose, and methods from region-to-image distillation to
Vision-OPD transfer such evidence to a full-image
model ( Wei et al., 2026 ; Yuan et al., 2026 ) . Subsequent work refines the selectivity
of this supervision through view-based reweighting ( Liu et al., 2026 ) , trajectory
gating ( Sun et al., 2026 ) , gradient decomposition ( Yoon et al., 2026 ) , modality
balance ( Aniri et al., 2026 ) , and target reconstruction ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , whereas VAG
uses a signed visual contrast to determine whether a candidate teacher
correction is admitted into policy optimization at all.

blocks.en: 2.2 Integrating RLVR with On-Policy Distillation
blocks.zh: 2.2 将RLVR与政策扭曲相结合

blocks.en:
RLVR anchors optimization to checkable outcomes, and GRPO realizes this without a learned
critic by estimating group-relative advantages that are nevertheless shared by
all tokens in a response ( Shao et al., 2024 ) . OPD supplies the missing token-level
resolution, yet its preference need not agree with trajectory
correctness, so the two signals are complementary but not automatically
compatible. Existing integrations reconcile them by weighting the two
objectives, restricting the teacher gap to modulating verifier-directed
magnitudes, gating implicit OPD rewards by trajectory correctness, or
contrasting privileged contexts ( Hübotter et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026 ; Pan et al., 2026 ) , while variants
route samples or tokens between the two objectives, account for student
uncertainty, or reverse teacher signals to encourage exploration ( Li et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026 ; Ke et al., 2026 ; Kim et al., 2026 ) . VAG
resolves this compatibility at the token level instead: a signed correction
enters the verifier-anchored advantage only when its direction agrees with the
visual evidence contrast, which preserves both visually supported promotion and
visually justified suppression while falling back to outcome supervision
whenever attribution fails.

blocks.en:
Given an image–question pair, VAG proceeds through the three-stage training
loop illustrated in Fig. 3 . In Stage 1
(Sec. 3.2 ), VAG derives a reliable trajectory-level
advantage from on-policy rollouts sampled by the frozen student policy and
scored by a task verifier. In Stage 2
(Sec. 3.3 ), the positive and negative teacher branches of
the same Exponential Moving Average (EMA) model replay each student-generated prefix under an
evidence-centered view and its random-masked counterpart, respectively. These
evaluations yield a teacher–student correction δ t \delta_{t} and a visual contrast v t v_{t} , whose sign agreement retains evidence-consistent token-level
supervision while filtering potentially contaminated corrections.
In Stage 3 (Sec. 3.4 ), VAG weights each retained
correction by its visual sensitivity and uses it to modulate, rather than
replace, the verifier advantage. The resulting token-level advantage is then
optimized using the clipped GRPO objective.

signal without discarding the verifier anchor of Stage 1.

Implementation Details .
We instantiate our method using Qwen3.5-4B ( Qwen Team, 2026 ) . The model is trained on a
curated synthetic dataset comprising approximately 6.2K visual-reasoning
examples derived from Vision-OPD ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) . During training, the
privileged teacher is maintained as an EMA of
the student parameters.
For all experiments, the student samples G = 8 G=8 on-policy responses for each

to 1,024 tokens. All models undergo full-parameter training for
one epoch and a 30-step warmup.
All experiments are conducted using 8 NVIDIA H800 GPUs.
Following the evaluation protocol of OPD-V ( Aniri et al., 2026 ) , we first perform deterministic answer matching, followed by a judge model that determines whether unresolved responses are correct by comparing them against the verified answer. For further details, see Appendices A and C .

blocks.en: 4.2 Baselines and Benchmarks
blocks.zh: 4.2 基线和基准

blocks.en:
Evaluation Benchmarks .
We evaluate VAG on six visual question answering benchmarks that span
fine-grained visual perception to broader multimodal problem solving. (1) V* Bench ( Wu and Xie, 2023 ) tests the localization and
recognition of small targets in high-resolution, visually crowded scenes. (2) ZoomBench ( Wei et al., 2026 ) examines
whether models can recover subtle regional evidence from a full image. (3) HR-Bench 4K and (4) HR-Bench 8K ( Wang et al., 2025 ) evaluate fine-grained
perception at native 4K and 8K resolutions, respectively.
These settings are particularly challenging
because conventional image resizing may discard the small-scale details required to answer the questions correctly. (5) MME-RealWorld EN and (6) MME-RealWorld CN ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) provide the broadest

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We introduce reinforcement learning with visually attributable on-policy self-distillation to mitigate privileged-correction contamination. Our Visual-Attribution Gating anchors optimization to verifier-derived trajectory advantages and accepts token-level corrections only when consistent with the contrast between evidence-present and evidence-degraded teacher views, preserving supportive and refuting visual evidence while suppressing inconsistent residuals. Across six public benchmarks, VAG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating that visual grounding verification unifies outcome verification, token-level self-distillation, and visual attribution for multimodal policy optimization.

Following OPD-V ( Aniri et al., 2026 ) , scoring proceeds in two stages. We first apply deterministic answer matching,
which resolves the majority of responses without any model in the loop. For the
multiple-choice benchmarks, a response counts as correct if it matches either the
answer text or the option letter, after normalizing surface variations such as
capitalization, surrounding punctuation, and common answer prefixes. Only the responses that
remain unresolved are passed to the second stage, where a Qwen3.5-series ( Qwen Team, 2026 ) model
acts as a binary Yes/No judge and decides whether the response is consistent
with the verified answer.

继OPD-V(Aniri等人,2026年)之后,分分两个阶段. 我们首先应用决定性的答案匹配,
解决大部分的响应 没有任何模式的循环。 对于
多重选择基准,如果符合

担任二进制是/否法官,并决定答复是否一致

blocks.en:
Both stages are necessary for the benchmarks we evaluate. Responses on
fine-grained perception tasks frequently state the correct answer inside a
longer justification, which deterministic matching alone would count as wrong;
delegating every response to the judge instead would introduce scoring variance
unrelated to the method under evaluation. Calling the judge only on the
unresolved responses therefore keeps most decisions exact while still absorbing
benign paraphrasing. Since the same protocol, judge model, and prompts apply to
every entry in Table 1 , the reported differences reflect the
trained policies rather than the evaluation.

The three image conditions differ only in the visual evidence they expose. The

blocks.en:
Fig. 7 reports two statistics throughout training: the mean verifier reward within each rollout group (left) and the mean response length (right).
The reward curve shows a clear upward trend, increasing from approximately 0.4 0.4 – 0.5 0.5 over the first twenty steps to 0.65 0.65 – 0.75 0.75 in the second half of training, before gradually stabilizing. This trend suggests that our training strategy consistently improves the policy while maintaining stable optimization in the later stages of training.

奖励曲线呈现出明显的上升趋势,从前20步的约0.4 – 0.5 0.5增长到后半步的0.65 0.65 – 0.75 0.75,然后逐渐稳定. 这一趋势表明,我们的培训战略不断改进政策,同时在培训的后期保持稳定的优化。

blocks.en: The response-length curve exhibits a different pattern. It oscillates within a relatively stable range throughout training and ends at a level comparable to its initial value, with no sustained growth. This is important because response-length inflation is a common confound in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards: a policy may increase its pass rate by producing longer responses that enumerate more candidate answers. In such cases, an increasing reward curve may reflect a change in response strategy rather than genuine improvement in visual perception.
blocks.zh: 响应长曲线显示不同的模式。 它在整个培训中在相对稳定的范围内振荡,其水平与初始价值相当,没有持续增长。 这一点很重要,因为反应长度的通货膨胀是强化学习和可核查的奖励的一个常见问题:一项政策可能会通过提出更长的答复来增加其通过率,其中列举更多的候选答案。 在这种情况下,奖励曲线增加可能反映反应战略的变化,而不是视觉感知的真正改善。
